title: D'IVOz Residences: shielded from Old Klang Road, a walk from Millerz.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #431 | D'IVOz RESIDENCES, OLD KLANG ROAD
excerpt: Two years after seeing it under construction, Sean returns to a project handed over ahead of schedule, where a creek park, a slip road and the pool deck shield the towers from Old Klang Road.
takeaways: Handed over ahead of schedule, with an internal slip road and buffers against Old Klang Road.
A 1,081 sq ft four-bedroom with a kitchen island, listed around RM585,000 and renting for about RM3,300 to RM3,500.
An untended riverbank behind, constant traffic, and four more projects launching nearby.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: D'IVOz sits behind a slip road, a landscaped creek park and a pool deck that push its two towers back from Old Klang Road; Tower B, nearer the river, is quieter. There are 10 units a floor sharing four lifts, no level changes from the drop-off to the front door, fire doors held open on magnets, and a pixelated paint scheme that hides plaster imperfections. Facilities include a cascading pool, a gym, two badminton courts and a rooftop with an edible garden and barbecue pits.

Sean viewed the 1,081 sq ft four-bedroom Type B1 handed over with an island, cabinets, hob, hood, microwave and aircon points. Its living space is 3.45 m wide, and a storage nook sits off the corridor.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: The project faces Old Klang Road opposite Pearl Point, among factories, standalone furniture shops, restaurants and new towers. The road leads to Taman Desa, Kuchai Lama, Puchong, Bukit Jalil, the Federal Highway and the city. Millerz mall is a five-minute walk, though not all of it is covered. Drivers from the KL side must U-turn further up the road to get home.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Listings for this layout range from about RM585,000, the common figure, to RM700,000. Fully furnished, it rents for about RM3,300 to RM3,500 a month against an instalment of around RM3,000 at RM600,000, which Sean calls sensible.

standout.title: No steps from car to front door
standout.body: From the drop-off through the lobby and corridors to each unit, every change in level is a gentle gradient rather than a step, even at the washrooms on the facility deck. Sean notes the developer's earlier projects still had drops, and that this is tedious to coordinate.

pros: The address: Old Klang Road connects to Taman Desa, Kuchai Lama, Puchong, the city and Bangsar South, with mature amenities. From this plot you can walk to Millerz, Pearl Point and other shops.
Design that answers the site: a slip road off Old Klang Road, the creek park and pool deck as buffers, unit doors placed out of each other's sight, and no level drops from the drop-off to the unit.

The developer's progress: what worked in earlier projects is kept, the landscaping is far richer, a convenience store opens at handover, and the project was delivered ahead of time despite the lockdowns.
cons: Design gaps: an untended riverbank with people passing behind Tower B, an awkward walk in for pedestrians, deep drains near the playground, and a four-bedroom layout with a corridor of doors and the common bathroom beside the master bedroom.
Old Klang Road traffic, busy all day; locals get used to it, newcomers may not. The slip road at least keeps queues off the main road.
Supply: four more projects are launching on this stretch, all selling well, and empty land remains, so check before buying for investment or own stay.

closing: Sean remains a fan of the developer's architecture, though he admits they may have overdone the details more than he would.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this March 2026 episode. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. Sean revisited the project about two years after a first visit during construction and viewed an empty unit soon after handover; prices are from property portal listings.
